key_insight: Staged closure learning trades moderately higher error for substantially fewer model evaluations and more robust optimization than embedded training.
engineering_relevance: Learning closures offline from assimilated trajectories can reduce training costs for reduced dynamical models by avoiding repeated simulator calls.
method: Compare embedded closure training with a two-stage data-assimilation approach.
Infer state and closure trajectories from observations, then train a machine learning closure offline.
Evaluate accuracy and computational cost on a synthetic SIQR epidemiological model with a nonlinear, state-dependent quarantine closure.
evidence_signal: In the synthetic SIQR evaluation, embedded training achieved the best average accuracy, while staged learning preserved comparable qualitative behavior with moderately higher error and substantially fewer model evaluations.
watch_item: The findings come from one synthetic exemplar, so the accuracy–efficiency trade-off may differ for other systems or observation conditions.
paper_title: Efficient Closure Learning in Dynamical Systems: A Comparison of Data-Assimilated and Embedded Approaches
